name: Desert Frost troop strength and battle membership
summary: World::troopStrength and placeInBattle separate a troop’s fighting strength from membership in the engagement.
adaptation: Use a scenario in which two otherwise similar troops differ in equipment or location. Compare participation and strength independently.
rights_note: The engine file carries its own GPL-3.0-or-later header. The top-level Apache notice covers a different scope. Original Dune data has separate terms.

name: Desert Frost troop movement between settlements
summary: World::unlinkTroop and linkTroop move a unit between settlement records. Equipment registration and encounters are separate operations.
adaptation: In a campaign-map tool, test transfer out, transfer in and entity deletion against both the old and new settlement lists.
rights_note: The engine file carries its own GPL-3.0-or-later header. The top-level Apache notice covers a different scope. Original Dune data has separate terms.

name: Save-menu cross-release regression harness
summary: The script exercises save-menu behavior across content variants and hashes fixtures during migration tests.
adaptation: Borrow the diagnostic pattern for a remake or mod that can open multiple editions. Test edition identification, temporary save slots and preservation of the original bytes.
rights_note: The top-level repository has an Apache license. Running the game-specific cases still requires the correct engine and content.

name: SwiftDune indexed palette and palette stash
summary: A fixed 256-color palette provides raw storage and a temporary stash for reversible palette changes.
adaptation: In a retro scene editor, preview an alternate palette without changing any sprite indices, then restore the original colors.
rights_note: The reviewed tree had no top-level license declaring redistribution terms for this Swift implementation. Study the design and seek permission before copying it.

name: SwiftDune pixel-buffer effects and sprite copy
summary: Rendering takes a destination buffer, effect and offset. Clearing and copying ranges are separate operations.
adaptation: Compare hard-edge masking and offset handling when an animation crosses a screen boundary. Keep original game sprites outside the test fixture.
